source_repository.evidence_scope: All 22 tracked files and all 12 commits were inspected. Findings distinguish repository evidence from current official documentation.
limitations: The repository has no README, tests, CI workflow or committed LICENSE file.
The package metadata declares ISC, but repository reuse terms should not be inferred beyond that package field.
Course video transcripts were not used for this revision.

architecture.classification_why: Retrieval always executes before generation; no model decides whether or how to retrieve. This matches LangChain's current definition of predictable 2-Step RAG.
architecture.goal: Answer questions about uploaded PDFs by retrieving semantically similar chunks and constraining an LLM with those chunks.

indexing.does: Accept one multipart PDF and stage it on disk.
indexing.why: The model cannot search a binary PDF directly; ingestion first establishes a bounded, typed document boundary.

indexing.does: Parse the PDF into LangChain Documents carrying page metadata.
indexing.why: Text and provenance must be extracted before semantic indexing; page metadata later supports traceable citations.

indexing.does: Split pages with chunkSize=1000 and chunkOverlap=200.
indexing.why: Whole pages can dilute relevant passages and exceed useful context granularity. Overlap preserves meaning that crosses chunk boundaries; 1000/200 is a baseline to evaluate, not a universal optimum.

indexing.does: Assign UUIDs plus documentId, chunkIndex, fileName, upload time and page.
indexing.why: Vector similarity alone cannot explain origin. Stable provenance fields enable source display, filtering, deletion and audit, although this sample uses random IDs and does not implement lifecycle operations.

indexing.does: Create text-embedding-3-small vectors for every chunk.
indexing.why: Embeddings place semantically related text near each other so queries can match concepts without exact keyword equality.

indexing.does: Persist 1536-dimensional vectors and text/provenance payloads in a Cosine collection.
indexing.why: A vector store makes nearest-neighbor retrieval persistent and scalable. Dimension 1536 matches the model's default; Cosine compares vector direction and Qdrant normalizes Cosine vectors on upload.

query.does: Require a trimmed 1..500 character question and topK 1..10 (default 3).
query.why: Input bounds prevent meaningless requests and cap retrieval/context cost before external services are called.

query.does: Embed the question with the same text-embedding-3-small model.
query.why: Document and query vectors must share the same vector space and dimension for similarity search to be meaningful.

query.does: Return topK nearest vectors with payload text and metadata.
query.why: Only likely relevant passages should consume the LLM context window. with_payload is required because vector IDs alone cannot ground an answer.

query.does: Join numbered result texts into one context block.
query.why: The generator needs a bounded evidence packet rather than the full corpus. Numbering gives the prompt a local reference structure.

query.does: Ask gpt-4o-mini at temperature 0 to answer in pt-BR using only context and to refuse if absent.
query.why: Retrieval supplies external knowledge; the system prompt narrows generation to evidence. Temperature 0 reduces variation but does not prove factuality or eliminate prompt injection.

query.does: Return fileName, chunkIndex and similarity score beside the answer.
query.why: Sources let clients inspect retrieval and are the minimum basis for citation validation, although page/documentId should also be returned.

serving.why: Separating ingestion, retrieval and generation makes each stage observable and independently testable.

serving.does: Emit sources, token and done JSON messages using text/event-stream.
serving.why: LLM generation is latency-heavy; streaming improves perceived latency and lets source metadata arrive before the complete answer.

serving.does: POST a question with fetch and read the response ReadableStream.
serving.why: Native EventSource cannot send a POST body, so fetch is appropriate for a question payload; the sample's additional unused EventSource is a defect, not a required pattern.

dependency_flow: answer -> JSON response or SSE sources/token/done stream

stack.role: ESM application runtime and type checking
stack.why: Async iteration is used for model streaming and ESM aligns with current package imports.
The course needs separate upload, search, answer and stream endpoints. Express 5 can forward rejected async handlers to error middleware when errors are not swallowed locally.

stack.role: PDF loading, recursive splitting, embeddings, prompt composition and streamed parsing
stack.why: It supplies replaceable interfaces for the standard RAG stages rather than coupling all providers in route handlers.
It is a cost-oriented semantic representation model. The vector collection dimension must remain coupled to the configured embedding dimension.
The sample chooses a cost/performance model and temperature 0 for less variable answers; model choice is not a retrieval-quality substitute.

stack.role: Persistent Cosine vector collection and payload retrieval
stack.why: It separates searchable semantic storage from the stateless API and supports future score thresholds, payload filters and indexes.
Uploads require a file-aware boundary; query and file metadata require runtime validation because TypeScript types disappear at runtime.

stack.role: One-way incremental answer delivery for POST questions
stack.why: The server only needs to push generation chunks after one client request, so WebSockets are unnecessary.

evolution.title: setup and configuration
evolution.why_now: Provision the external contracts and fail startup if the vector store cannot initialize; later ingestion and queries depend on a consistent model/store schema.

evolution.title: file upload middleware and response types
evolution.why_now: Establish a bounded input adapter before implementing expensive parsing and embeddings.

evolution.title: document upload route and processing service
evolution.why_now: Complete the indexing half so a searchable corpus exists before retrieval is exposed.

evolution.title: uploads configuration and directory bootstrap
evolution.why_now: Make the filesystem assumption explicit and prevent the first upload from failing because its staging directory does not exist.

evolution.title: dependencies and Nike 10-K fixture
evolution.why_now: Exercise semantic retrieval against a non-trivial document with pages, tables and repeated financial language.

evolution.title: query router and vector search
evolution.why_now: Validate retrieval quality independently before adding generation; bad retrieval cannot be repaired reliably by prompting.

evolution.title: RAG router and context-based answers
evolution.why_now: Add generation only after retrieval works, producing the canonical retrieve-then-generate 2-Step RAG flow.

evolution.title: OpenAI retries and timeouts
evolution.why_now: External model calls can fail or stall; bounded retries tolerate transient faults while timeouts prevent indefinite requests.

evolution.title: error handling and validation
evolution.why_now: Move boundary checks out of route business logic and distinguish client errors from unexpected server failures.

evolution.title: SSE RAG streaming
evolution.why_now: Reduce perceived answer latency and expose provenance before generation completes without introducing bidirectional WebSockets.

evolution.title: browser chat sample
evolution.why_now: Demonstrate the wire protocol and prove that SSE-framed POST responses can be consumed in a browser.

evolution.title: CORS and final dependencies
evolution.why_now: Allow the standalone sample UI to call the API from another origin; wildcard CORS is demonstration configuration, not a production default.

file_map.why: Model, Qdrant, server and upload configuration must stay consistent across stages; startup fails closed when OPENAI_API_KEY is absent.
One embedding instance guarantees document/query model consistency; one deterministic chat instance centralizes retry and timeout policy.
The collection must exist with a dimension and metric compatible with generated embeddings before writes or searches.
Parsing, chunking, metadata, embedding and upsert form one ordered data transformation with explicit failure checks.
Separating search from generation makes Recall@k, score distributions and metadata correctness independently testable.
The prompt and parser are generation policy; they consume retrieval results but should not own vector storage.
Routes translate transport inputs/outputs while services retain domain sequencing.
Static types do not validate JSON or multipart requests; Zod supplies executable bounds.

file_map.responsibility: Cross-cutting upload, validation and error policy
file_map.why: Shared boundary behavior should not be repeated across endpoints.
A minimal client validates source-first and token-by-token rendering without requiring a frontend framework.

production_gaps.finding: No score_threshold or relevance sufficiency gate; unrelated topK chunks still reach the LLM.
production_gaps.why_it_matters: TopK always returns nearest items even when all are weak. Prompt-only refusal is nondeterministic.
production_gaps.improvement: Calibrate a threshold on an evaluation set, pass score_threshold to Qdrant, and refuse before generation when evidence is insufficient.

production_gaps.finding: No authentication, tenant/ACL metadata filters, rate limits or upload ownership.
production_gaps.why_it_matters: A shared collection can leak one user's document chunks into another user's answer.
production_gaps.improvement: Authenticate every route; include tenantId/document ACL in payload; create payload indexes before ingestion; enforce filters inside vector search.

production_gaps.finding: Retrieved PDF text is inserted directly into the LLM context without output verification.
production_gaps.why_it_matters: Documents can contain indirect instructions that compete with application instructions; delimiters alone do not reliably prevent this.
production_gaps.improvement: Treat chunks explicitly as untrusted data, minimize tool authority, validate citations/claims against retrieved chunks and test injection fixtures.

production_gaps.finding: validateFile calls CommonJS require inside an ESM application.
production_gaps.why_it_matters: require is not defined in native ESM, so upload validation can fail at runtime.
production_gaps.improvement: Statically import fileUploadSchema at module top.

production_gaps.finding: The code directly imports @langchain/openai and @langchain/textsplitters, but package.json does not declare them directly.
production_gaps.why_it_matters: Transitive dependency hoisting is not a stable application contract and can break after lockfile or package-manager changes.
production_gaps.improvement: Declare every directly imported package in dependencies and verify with a clean npm install/build.

production_gaps.finding: Existing Qdrant collections are accepted without checking vector size, distance or embedding model version.
production_gaps.why_it_matters: Changing model or dimensions can cause write errors or semantic incompatibility.
production_gaps.improvement: Version collection names or validate schema/model metadata at startup; reindex on incompatible changes.

production_gaps.finding: Random IDs make every re-upload additive; there is no deduplication, update, delete or tombstone path.
production_gaps.why_it_matters: Duplicate chunks distort retrieval and retained documents cannot be governed.
production_gaps.improvement: Use content hashes/stable chunk IDs, idempotent upserts and document-scoped delete/reindex operations.

production_gaps.finding: The prompt requests document_id citations but packed context contains numeric labels and the API source list omits documentId/page.
production_gaps.why_it_matters: The model lacks a consistent citation identifier and clients cannot verify a claim at page level.
production_gaps.improvement: Pack explicit source headers with documentId, fileName, page and chunkIndex; validate every emitted citation.

production_gaps.finding: sample/chat.html opens an unused EventSource and then separately sends fetch; it parses each network chunk as complete lines.
production_gaps.why_it_matters: The unused connection hits a POST-only route with GET, and SSE frames can split across ReadableStream chunks causing JSON parse failures.
production_gaps.improvement: Use fetch only, buffer decoded text until complete blank-line-delimited SSE messages, handle response.ok, AbortController and decoder flush.
evidence: MDN SSE and Fetch streaming docs

production_gaps.finding: No disconnect cancellation, heartbeat, explicit flush or headers-sent error delegation.
production_gaps.why_it_matters: Generation may continue after clients leave; proxies may buffer or time out; streaming failures need different handling after headers.
production_gaps.improvement: Cancel on request close, emit heartbeat comments, call flushHeaders when available, disable proxy buffering and follow Express headersSent guidance.

production_gaps.why_it_matters: Wildcard access is convenient for a sample but broadens browser access to an API that has no authentication.
production_gaps.improvement: Allowlist deployment origins and combine CORS with authentication; CORS is not authorization.

production_gaps.finding: No automated tests, retrieval evaluation set, observability traces or CI.
production_gaps.why_it_matters: Chunking, model, prompt or dependency changes can silently reduce Recall@k, groundedness and citation validity.
production_gaps.improvement: Add unit/integration tests plus a labeled query corpus measuring Recall@k, MRR/nDCG, answer correctness, groundedness, citation validity, latency and cost.
